validations.droid_claim:
[P0] `queued` default timestamp is evaluated at import time

`queued: datetime = timezone.now()` is evaluated once when the module is imported, so every `AssignmentSource` created without an explicit `queued` will share the same stale timestamp. Use `dataclasses.field(default_factory=timezone.now)` so `timezone.now()` runs per instance.
validations.impact: All AssignmentSource instances created via from_integration() share the same stale queued timestamp from module import time, causing incorrect temporal ordering of assignment events.
validations.reasoning: Line 18 defines `queued: datetime = timezone.now()` as a dataclass field default. In Python dataclasses, default values are evaluated once at class definition time (module import), not per-instance. The from_integration() classmethod on line 21-25 calls AssignmentSource(source_name=..., integration_id=...) without passing queued, so it relies on this stale default. This is confirmed by checking callers in sync.py lines 98 and 115 which both use from_integration(). The fix is exactly as the Droid suggests: use `field(default_factory=timezone.now)`.
